messages:
Mike (Sales): Hey team — prepping the POC kickoff with Nimbus Bank tomorrow. They asked for a short checklist: how we want sample data delivered, redaction expectations, connectivity options, and what constitutes POC success. Can we align quickly?
Amy (SE): +1. Core asks from Nimbus: 1) run 3 core flows (acct summarization, fraud flagging prompts, KYC extraction) 2) compare latency/cost vs their current infra 3) data never leaves their VPC unless encrypted/approved.
Jordan (Eng): For sandbox options we can do one of: a) S3 presigned ingestion + redaction pipeline in our staging, b) VPC peering with Dedicated test pool, c) upload to a TEMP encrypted bucket in their account and we run inference via cross-account role. Tradeoffs: a is fastest to set up, b is best for security/latency.
Tara (Security): If they want data in their VPC (option b), we need the network diagram, an allowlist of subnets, and their KMS ARN for CMK cross-account decrypt. Also need to confirm no PHI in sample data or ensure we apply redaction.
Mike (Sales): They said they can only share obfuscated records but may include account numbers masked. Is that OK for our evals?
Amy (SE): Masked account numbers fine for KYC extraction if we treat them as token placeholders. For fraud flows we need patterns preserved (e.g., sequence of tx amounts/timestamps). Recommend they send 100–500 anonymized records per flow.
Jordan (Eng): Quick redaction snippet we can provide them to run locally before upload:
```
# simple PII scrubbing
python redact.py --in sample.csv --out sample_redacted.csv --fields name,email,ssn --mask-with <REDACTED>
```
Share `redact.py` from our repo; it keeps original schema so evals run unchanged.
Tara (Security): Also add a SHA256 checksum field for each file and require uploads over TLS. We need an auditable retention policy: sandbox data auto-delete after 30 days unless legal extends.
infra-bot: NOTE: For VPC peering we require a support ticket with subnet CIDR and the peering window is ~48–72h once network details are provided.
Mike (Sales): Pricing question from procurement: will this POC incur infra charges or is it covered by the credit? They asked for an estimate for Dedicated test pool for 2 weeks.
Amy (SE): Ballpark: a small dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) for 2 weeks ~= $Xk — I'll pull exact numbers. But we can run a hosted sandbox using burst credits for free if they accept slightly higher tail latency.
Jordan (Eng): Success criteria proposal: 1) functional: all 3 flows pass accuracy thresholds (precision>90% for KYC fields, fraud recall >85% on flagged set) 2) perf: median latency <350ms per request for summarize flow 3) infra: data stored encrypted and deleted after 30d. If they agree we'll script eval harness and dashboards.
Tara (Security): Add requirement: keys never exported; logs sanitized. We'll sign an NDA for sample dataset if they want.
Mike (Sales): Great. I'll consolidate and send Nimbus a one-pager with options A/B/C, required artifacts (sample files, network diagram, KMS ARN), timeline (2w setup + 2w run), and success criteria. @Amy can you drop the eval checklist and the `redact.py` link into the doc by EOD?
Amy (SE): On it. I'll include a minimal eval script, expected file schema, and a template CSV with 10 anonymized rows.
Jordan (Eng): I'll add the infra steps and the peering support ticket template.
Tara (Security): I'll draft the security addendum for the POC and note retention + key rules.
Mike (Sales): Thanks — once I have the doc I'll ping Nimbus and get their sample files. If they prefer presigned S3 upload we should provide a small curl example.
Amy (SE): Example presigned upload: `curl -X PUT "${PRESIGNED_URL}" -T sample_redacted.csv --header "x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms"`
Mike (Sales): Perfect. Closing loop later today. :thumbsup:
